player_note: NicolaiBolas drafts; the guest Alex Nikolic (LLU) advises. 'speaker' = guest, host or both (captions unlabelled).
source: YouTube auto-caption transcript 0:00-33:35 (tools/video_draft.py transcript 8BzUchj9HuA --start 0 --end 2015), card names corrected against data/Sets/FRA_PremierDraft_All_Data.json; nothing past 33:35 read. 'type' marks each idea as claim, heuristic or one-off pick; 'repeats' lists ideas of earlier videos it restates; 'related' lists looser topic matches.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Reality Fracture is balanced: you do not have to be in one colour or avoid another, and drafts do not feel like the same thing each time.
ideas.quote: You don't feel like, oh, you got to be in this color or you really want to avoid this color.
ideas.test_idea: Spread of deck win rate across colour pairs compared with the spread within a pair, by skill.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: His own favourite decks are green-red ramp (Kiora, the green-red uncommon) and, to win a draft, blue-white surveil aggro.
ideas.quote: if I really wanted to win this draft, what would I be in? I think Blue White Surveil Aggro is probably my number one pick there.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of blue-white against green-red decks by skill group.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Murmuring Volume is underrated: a colourless mana rock with rummage that does duty on both filtering and getting to big things in ramp decks.
ideas.quote: Murmuring volume, the mana rock that you pay two to rummage. Big fan of that card in the ramp decks.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Murmuring Volume in ramp decks.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Archive Arbiter (six-mana 4/4 flier that destroys a noncreature, nonland permanent or gains four life) is very playable and he gets it last pick.
ideas.quote: That card is I think very very playable and I get a last pick
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Archive Arbiter and its ALSA.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Monocoloured over gold is an upside when close, but he is not afraid of strong gold cards; there are many in this set.
ideas.quote: as always, I think monocolored over gold is definitely an upside. So, if it's close, I like taking the monocolor card, but I'm not afraid of taking the strong gold cards.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of gold cards against mono-coloured cards at equal pick position; fraction of gold picks that reach the final colours.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Recursive Recruitment is a phenomenal card: pretty good on four, really good late, can be self-milled to draw it free, or rummaged away for value; it plays well with any self-mill.
ideas.quote: I think this card is phenomenal. It's just, you know, pretty good on four, really good late.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Recursive Recruitment by number of self-mill cards in the deck.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Primal Witchstalker is a card he has been super impressed with: three-mana 2/1 menace that ramps, sometimes a three-for-one (body, land, a milled flashback card).
ideas.quote: sometimes it's like a three for one almost because you get the body, you get a land, and you mill a flashback card or something.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Primal Witchstalker in green decks.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Prophesied End is better than the typical destroy-tapped or destroy-attacking removal: in aggressive decks you can kill the big blocker on the last turn and the card draw does not matter.
ideas.quote: in the aggressive decks you do like the ability to in the last turn of the game say okay I kill your big blocker you draw a card doesn't matter you're dead.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Prophesied End in aggro decks.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Read signals from the whole pack, not one card: three red cards in a row and a Pia in a pack, but the colours that pair with green are not coming, so the open colour is unclear; the set is powerful enough that you need not be in the most open lane.
ideas.quote: I haven't really felt like I needed to be in the most open lane to get a good deck.
ideas.test_idea: Whether being in the most open lane improves deck win rate in FRA, controlling for skill.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Land cyclers are really good: they fix and are good cards to cast; he has been high on them all set.
ideas.quote: I've been really high on land cyclingers. They're just really really good at fixing you and they're all good cards.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of the landcycler cycle by colour.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Add colours to layer synergies rather than only for raw power: white for Generous Revival in a graveyard deck.
ideas.quote: I don't mind adding colors, not necessarily even for omega powerful cards, but to layer on your synergies.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of decks with a synergy-driven third colour against two-colour decks.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Take good spells over fixing in pack one, because the set has plenty of fixing.
ideas.quote: I've been taking good spells over fixing in pack one anyways.
ideas.test_idea: Play rate of lands taken in picks 1 to 8 of pack 1; GIH WR of cards passed for them.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: A card like Paradox Shaper is not worth taking over a land when other cards help mill better; the red cards do not play well with their green cards.
ideas.quote: It's a nice tool to have the Shaper. But there's other better cards that help you mill.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Paradox Shaper vs lands taken at pick 8.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Splash fishing removal like Surgical Precision when the deck has none.
ideas.quote: we don't have any removal right now and I've been happy to splash removal like fishing removal like this one.
ideas.test_idea: Splash win rate of Surgical Precision.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Do not be strict about colour-pair themes: his green-white decks have been go-wide rather than life gain; look at what your cards ask you to do.
ideas.quote: I don't think you have to be super strict about the color pair theming in this set.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of green-white decks by number of life-gain cards.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Guiding Hydra over Your Fate Ends Here: the higher-upside card, but he could regret it without removal; the host notes they will probably get a removal spell back from the pack.
ideas.quote: I would go for the higher upside card right now, but I could see us maybe regretting this if we maybe don't see as much removal as we'd like.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Guiding Hydra against Your Fate Ends Here.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Unsummon has been really good against beast tokens and Kiora dragon tokens: a lot of big tokens to bounce.
ideas.quote: It's been really good against the beast tokens or the Kiora Dragon tokens.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Unsummon against opponents' token-making cards.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Something Worth Saving is good for finding the great cards while binning flashback cards, since there is a big gap between the great and the medium cards; in a deck that is not graveyard focused he wants only one copy.
ideas.quote: just being able to find your good cards while binning flashback cards has been something I liked.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Something Worth Saving by copy count and graveyard density.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Prefer the colourless two-drop in pack two so that you can take better expensive cards in pack three; it also doubles as a best-of-three sideboard card.
ideas.quote: this lets us take better expensive cards in pack three.
ideas.test_idea: Play rate and GIH WR of Afterthought Sentry.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Twisted Fates is a card he is a huge fan of, particularly when low on removal and with the fixing to cast it.
ideas.quote: Huge fan of Twisted Fates and huge fan of it here where we're a little bit low on removal.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Twisted Fates as a splash.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Way of the Healer over a green-white gold card: ask what your deck is doing; they are not a life-gain deck, so the gold card is not for them and Healer helps them go wide.
ideas.quote: This is a perfect example of what is your deck doing.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Bloombrute by number of life-gain cards in the deck.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: In best of three, sideboard cards are worth taking pretty highly because they are a huge upgrade over a game-one card; he picks the sideboard card over a land.
ideas.quote: I take these sideboard cards pretty highly when I'm drafting best of three.
ideas.test_idea: Not testable on 17Lands best-of-one data; record only.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Cut Restore with Empathy and Fateshaper Aspirant first: the Aspirant returns few legends in a deck that does not lose its Healers; Restore only belongs in a graveyard deck.
ideas.quote: if we were in the graveyard deck, I would play it, but not for this deck so much.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Fateshaper Aspirant; play rate of Restore with Empathy outside graveyard decks.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Aim for one Swamp only: the mana has double green and double white, so a second Swamp for the Twisted Fates splash would hurt.
ideas.quote: we have double green, double whites, and a swamp in there. So, I would definitely would like to not play a second swamp.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of splash-two-cards decks by source count with double-pip base colours.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: A landcycler you will not cast (a Witchstalker) is not worth playing just for the cycling; play a land instead if there is fixing already.
ideas.quote: if we're not planning to cast the witchstalker basically ever, it's not really going to pull its weight so much.
ideas.test_idea: Play rate of landcyclers by colour fit.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Titanbones, Towering Heart needs a lot of life gain to be worth the card: Hortimancer is a two-mana 2/1 that can trade early, while the four-mana 4/3 with no enters effect must get huge all the time.
ideas.quote: I need that thing to be getting huge all the time for it to be worth the card.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Titanbones, Towering Heart by life-gain count.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Ferocity of the Hunt is not great in a deck with tokens: a death or enters effect on a token does not help; he checks for death triggers or enters effects before a trick.
ideas.quote: I'm just imagining a scenario where we have our combat trick and we have a perfect spot to use it and we can't because we have like our way of the healer token.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Ferocity of the Hunt by token count.

ideas.speaker: Alex Nikolic (guest)
ideas.claim: Cut a two-drop for a deck that builds out the board and sits back: the Sentry is a plain two-mana 2/2 against decks that ignore the graveyard, and Teyo can be flashed in as a two-mana 2/2.
ideas.quote: this is more of a build out the board kind of creature deck where we don't mind just sitting back
ideas.test_idea: Two-drop count against win rate in go-wide decks.
